newsitem.title: USA: Vapors spread from capsized barge in Baton Rouge.
newsitem.headline: Vapors spread from capsized barge in Baton Rouge.

text.p: Changing winds spread noxious vapors from a capsized tanker barge in the Mississippi River on Tuesday night, prompting officials to suspend classes and evacuate students from Southern University.

Coast Guard Capt. Gordon Marsh told Reuters that the barge, carrying an aromatic gasoline with a high benzene content, was continuing to leak in small amounts and traces of chemical vapors were detected on both banks of the river north of the accident site.
The barge that overturned at about 5 p.m. CST (6 p.m. EST) Monday was one of 25 under tow that struck a bridge in north Baton Rouge and broke loose.

Baton Rouge police spokesman Don Kelly said the evacuations from the university, about a mile from the capsized barge, were voluntary. But he said residents within a two-mile radius were ordered to either leave or shelter in place by shutting off air conditioners and closing windows and doors.
Marsh said cranes will try to right the barge and off-load it Wednesday morning.
The evacuating students were bused to the Louisiana State University Field House across town. Police said no injuries had been reported.

The Mississippi River has been closed while workers clean up after the barges hit the bridge. Two rock barges sank, two were beached and one was missing, while the tanker barge carrying a mix of benzene and gasoline capsized and was aground on the west bank of the river.
